_comment: Declarative execution pipeline. Stage commands use placeholders resolved from .agentry/project/stack.md during interactive onboarding (see _init-prompt.md Phase B). The deterministic hooks (tools/pipeline/*.py) read this file; the model never decides a transition.

workflow._comment: What kind of project this is, read by tools/pipeline/pretool_gate.py. mode 'pr' (DEFAULT when absent) is the collaborative shape: nothing commits on the trunk, the branch is pushed and a human opens the pull request. mode 'solo' is the single-author shape: there is no second party to review or merge, so a LOCAL `git merge` of an approved task branch into the trunk is allowed - the task must still match <type>/task-NNNN, have a row in run.db, and carry an approved commit checkpoint, because those guard against merging unreviewed work rather than against working alone. Pushing to a protected branch is refused in BOTH modes. push_needs_approval is independent of the mode (default true): working alone says nothing about whether an unattended run may write to the remote. See .claude/rules/git-workflow.md.

memory._comment: Post-task memory review gate (tools/memory/update.py): every done task above baseline must be distilled into .agentry/memory/ (lessons/patterns/codebase rows) and stamped before the next task starts. Enforced by stop_gate.py. baseline semantics match handoff.baseline; '' = every done task covered. enabled=false disables the gate.

orchestrator_gate._comment: Hard gate on the MAIN THREAD (orchestrator): Edit/Write and shell file-writes are denied outside .claude/, .agentry/, docs/, README*, root CLAUDE.md. The orchestrator only formalizes tasks, delegates, verifies and synthesizes - it never authors code. Subagent tool calls are exempt (agent_gate.py profiles govern them). extra_allow: repo-relative globs to whitelist per project (e.g. "CHANGELOG.md"). enabled=false disables the gate.

gates._comment: Stack-specific denials read by tools/pipeline/{pretool_gate,agent_gate}.py. Filled during onboarding (see _init-prompt.md Phase B) from the detected language/framework so the gate CODE stays language-agnostic. Empty array / false / '' disables that gate. Generic gates (branch base+naming, AI-attribution in commits, em/en dash, writes under ~/.claude) need no config and always run.

handoff._comment: Forced context-absorption chain: before any NEW task registers, every done task with id above baseline must have a valid doc in dir. The doc is written by the NEXT task's assignee in its own words. baseline: '' for a fresh project (every done task covered); when adopting mid-project, set it at onboarding to the highest pre-existing done task id (those are grandfathered). Enforced by advance.py (registration refusal), stop_gate.py (start-next-task block) and pretool_gate.py (hard_edit_gate code-edit freeze). Tools: handoff.py --check / --for / --waive (waive is orchestrator-only, CEO approval required).

supervisor._comment: External supervisor (tools/pipeline/supervisor.py) - a process with its own clock, started DETACHED by the SessionStart hook (supervisor.py --ensure-running) and a singleton per lane, because a watcher that dies with the session cannot report that session's death. Stop it with supervisor.py --stop. It polls run.db plus the task folders, classifies every in-flight run HEALTHY / STALLED / LOOPING / DEAD from observed facts, relaunches STALLED and DEAD work as a headless session, and parks LOOPING work blocked. LOOPING is NEVER relaunched and there is no key here that can change that. stall_seconds: no change to the STAGE for this long, with no other evidence, is a stall (keep it above a slow exit gate - advance.py's own gate timeout is 900s). There is deliberately no loop_ticks key: task-0067 measured that reading firing on ordinary work (a 60s turn cycle parked a live task in three minutes) and deleted it, leaving the pipeline's own continuation_ceiling as the loop budget. idle_exit_polls: consecutive polls with nothing in flight after which the daemon exits and releases its lock (0 never exits). spawn_cmd: argv, never a shell string; placeholders {task} {stage} {prompt}. Both caps are hard - exceeding either stops the supervisor and notifies. enabled=false makes it exit without looking, and makes the SessionStart hook a no-op.

build._comment: Implementation. Drives a task from code to a pushed branch. Merging into the main branch is always the CEO's, never the agent's.

stages.name: test
stages._comment: ui_evidence: true appends 'python .claude/tools/pipeline/ui_evidence.py --task {task}' to the exit gate at onboarding, so UI-touching tasks require real-browser evidence in .agentry/state/evidence/<task>.json. Set false for API-only projects.

stages.name: ready
stages._comment: auto_approve: checkpoints listed here (e.g. ["commit"] or ["commit", "push"]) are approved by advance.py itself - no CEO parking. Empty = both approvals stay manual. Decide at onboarding Phase B; changing it later is a CEO decision.

plan._comment: Design. Turns a request into an approved plan, a spec and task files sitting in tasks/backlog/. Writes documents, never product code.

stages.name: formalize
stages._comment: Write the problem statement: what hurts, scope, non-goals, open questions. Parks on the CEO until the questions are answered - that information exists nowhere else.

stages.name: plan-review
stages._comment: Read-only review of the plan itself. Critical and High findings must be closed before approval.

stages.name: approval
stages._comment: CEO approves the plan. A plan is dearer than code: one wrong assumption is copied into every task below it.

stages.name: breakdown
stages._comment: Spec with testable acceptance criteria, then task files written into tasks/backlog/. A spec that is not sliced into tasks is half done.
